basic_info.name: Levels (Levels Health; levels.com / levelshealth.com)
basic_info.category: Metabolic health membership platform: CGM biosensor + at-home/lab blood testing + behavior-change app (wearable-adjacent D2C health)
basic_info.stage: Growth-stage private startup. Founded 2019 (founded by Josh Clemente, Dr. Casey Means, Sam Corcos, Dan Zavorotny; TechCrunch Nov 2020 lists Clemente as CEO, Means as co-founder). Still active and shipping in Aug 2026; reportedly profitable in recent years [uncertain]. Co-founder Casey Means was nominated US Surgeon General in May 2025 (nomination withdrawn April 2026), giving the brand outsized visibility.
basic_info.pricing_model: Three-tier membership (as of Aug 2026, captured from live site): (1) 'Build your system' — app only, $15/mo or $80 billed annually; CGM, labs and experts added a-la-carte. (2) 'Core' — $41/mo or $499/yr: Levels app + AI health insights + adaptive programs, 2 Essential Lab Panels (28+ markers), 1 month of continuous glucose monitoring, clinician review of health data 2x/year, unlimited upload of past bloodwork. (3) 'Complete' — $167/mo or $1,999/yr: everything in Core plus 2 Comprehensive Lab Panels (100+ markers), 2 months of CGM with free shipping, 50-minute functional nutritionist session, dedicated concierge support, advanced AI insights. All tiers HSA/FSA eligible via Truemed (~30% average savings). A-la-carte add-ons: extra glucose monitors, comprehensive labs, dietitian sessions. Price history: launched ~2020 with a 4-week CGM program (~$199-396), later restructured into an all-inclusive membership (~$199/mo or ~$1,990/yr circa 2023) before the current 3-tier split with a low-price app entry tier [uncertain — older price points from memory/secondary coverage, not re-verified]. No insurance coverage; dietitian coaching reportedly billable to insurance for most members (company claim).
basic_info.target_user: Health optimizers/biohackers and wellness-focused consumers who self-pay; large sub-segment with prediabetes/type-2 risk (biomarker report targets HbA1c 5.7-6.4%, high fasting insulin, high triglycerides). Not aimed at clinicians — patient D2C only.
basic_info.scale_metrics: Durable traction: '60,000+ members' (levelshealth.com homepage variant) and '100,000+ lives changed' (levels.com homepage variant, Aug 2026); 4.7 app-store-style rating claimed on site. Funding: $12M seed (Nov 2020) led by Andreessen Horowitz with Marc Randolph, Dick Costolo, Michael Arrington, Matt Dellavedova (TechCrunch); a further ~$38M round reported around 2021, total ~$50M raised [uncertain — aggregators blocked, not re-verified]; valuation undisclosed. Internal biomarker cohort sizes (n=894 HbA1c, n=492-164 fasting insulin, n=370 triglycerides) indicate tens of thousands of members doing repeat labs through Levels Labs — real recurring revenue, not hype. Self-reported claims of profitability and revenue ~$30M+ [uncertain].

product.core_features: Real-time glucose streaming from a Dexcom Stelo biosensor into the Levels app (support center is now entirely Stelo-based; marketing also references Dexcom G7; 'use Levels with your own CGM' BYO flow). AI food logging by text description, photo, or barcode with macro breakdowns and food-quality feedback. Habit tracking ('Habit Loops', metabolic checklist) across sleep, movement, meal timing, routines. Guided adaptive Programs (glucose control, heart health, weight loss) with adherence and progress tracking/challenges. Levels Labs blood panels: Essential 28+ markers, Comprehensive 100+ markers across ~15 categories (metabolic: HbA1c/fasting glucose/fasting insulin/uric acid; cardiovascular: ApoB/triglycerides +7 more; liver 9; kidney 6; thyroid 6; male 10 / female 8 hormones incl. AMH; nutrients 19; immune 6; stress & aging 3 incl. cortisol; pancreas 2; blood 8; urine 27; electrolytes 4). Clinician analysis and action plan 2x/year. Functional nutritionist 1:1 session (Complete tier). Upload of prior labs, DEXA scans and health records. Wearable import for exercise/sleep context. Long-term trends dashboard. LevelsAI search chatbot on blog/content.
product.signature_differentiator: The closed real-time feedback loop meal -> glucose curve -> scored outcome -> suggested swap, at population scale. Levels claims 'one of the largest proprietary metabolic datasets of its kind' / 'one of the largest observational glucose studies ever conducted in people without diabetes', which powers personalized food scoring and insights ('your body isn't generic; ours isn't advice'). They position themselves as 'the company that brought glucose monitoring into everyday metabolic health' — first mover in mainstreaming CGM for non-diabetics, now with the FDA OTC-cleared Stelo removing the prescription barrier entirely.
product.lab_data_handling: Three-layer cadence: (1) continuous — CGM sensor worn on the arm (~15-day Stelo; membership includes 1-2 months of monitoring per year, more a-la-carte); (2) periodic — 2 blood panels per year included in Core/Complete (28+ or 100+ markers), results integrate automatically into the app; company encourages retesting 'every few months' a-la-carte, with a formal reassessment + clinical analysis ~the 6-month mark; (3) retrospective — unlimited upload of past bloodwork (PDF/records), DEXA scans and health records. Interpretation is own-stack: algorithmic scoring in-app (basal glucose, glucose variability, insulin sensitivity, post-meal dynamics) plus licensed 'Levels-verified' clinician human review of labs 2x/year. Draw method (at-home phlebotomy vs Quest drops) not stated on site [uncertain]. No external lab integration for ingestion — you upload or buy their panel.
product.family_dependents_depth: None. Strictly single-user accounts: no dependent profiles, no caregiver mode, no pediatric reference ranges, no hereditary/family-risk features. The only 'sharing' artifact is a support article about physically sharing Stelo biosensor boxes with another person (hardware logistics, not family data). This remains a wide-open gap (and a Dr. Exame pillar no US player exploits).
product.doctor_sharing: Basic. From the member portal: 'Share Your Data' -> 'Share Your Health Data' -> enter the doctor/care-team member's email -> 'Grant Access' (viewer access to the dashboard). Separate self-service 'How to Export Your Data' article. Internally, a licensed clinician produces a detailed analysis + action plan 2x/year and (Complete tier) a functional nutritionist reviews all data before a 50-min session. But there is no structured consult brief, no SOAP-style summary, no doctor-facing portal or workflow — your own doctor gets read-only access, nothing more.
product.action_loop_monetization: The action loop IS the product: after interpretation, members keep paying for the membership that bundles hardware (CGMs), testing (2 lab panels/yr), humans (clinician review 2x/yr, nutritionist/dietitian add-ons, concierge) and behavior programs (guided goals with adherence tracking). No supplement marketplace, no prescriptions or telemedicine Rx, no imaging/MCED marketplace — margin sits in recurring subscription + a-la-carte sensors/labs/expert time, softened by HSA/FSA (Truemed) eligibility. Historically 4-week CGM 'challenges' were the entry product; now the cheap app tier ($80/yr) funnels into hardware/lab upsells.

technology.ai_approach: Hybrid: (a) AI/LLM food logging — describe the meal in text, snap a photo, or scan a barcode, and the app returns macros and food-quality feedback; (b) 'AI health insights' / tier-gated 'advanced AI health insights' engines that turn glucose + lab + nutrition patterns into next-step guidance, explicitly leveraging the aggregated proprietary metabolic dataset ('largest of its kind'); (c) LevelsAI, a public-facing AI search/chat over their content library; (d) classical algorithmic scoring of glucose dynamics (basal glucose, variability, insulin-sensitivity index, post-meal dynamics) and per-meal scoring. Human-in-the-loop: licensed clinician reviews lab data and writes the action plan. No published model/methodology details — scoring formulas are proprietary; peer-reviewed validation absent [uncertain whether any internal methodology paper exists].
technology.data_inputs: CGM glucose streams (Dexcom Stelo/G7, or bring-your-own CGM); Levels Labs blood panels; uploaded prior bloodwork/DEXA scans/health records; food logs (text/photo/barcode); wearable exercise and sleep data; comprehensive intake questionnaire (goals, history, context).
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: wearable data import for exercise/sleep (specific platforms not listed on current site — historically Apple Health and others [uncertain]); file upload of past labs and DEXA (PDF/records); CGM data via Dexcom integration. Exhaust: member-portal viewer sharing via email grant; self-service data export (support-documented). No public FHIR API, no Apple Health Records / Health Connect medical-records surface, no LIS/lab-partner integration, no WhatsApp — ingestion is broad-ish (files + wearables) but everything else is a closed app. Privacy policy hosted on Notion; HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2-compliant claims on homepage.
technology.platform: iOS/Android mobile app + web member portal (app.levels.com) + marketing/content site (levels.com, levelshealth.com) + support center (support.levels.com). No public developer API.

ux.onboarding: Quiz-first: app.levels.com/quiz gives a 'personalized plan' recommendation before checkout (used as the primary CTA site-wide). Then an 8-step journey: (1) comprehensive intake defining goals; (2) receive glucose monitor, set up 'in minutes', sync, see real-time data; (3) complete lab panel (results auto-integrate); (4) clinician analysis + action plan; (5) in-app personalized program; (6) advanced insights; (7) functional nutritionist session (Complete); (8) ~6-month reassessment with clinical analysis. Time-to-value is tiered: app logging/habit loops immediate; glucose feedback within days of sensor shipping; lab-based insights weeks.
ux.data_visualization: Real-time glucose curve overlaid with meals, exercise, sleep; per-meal scoring ('that morning oatmeal spiked you to 150 — try chia pudding') with smart-swap suggestions; macro breakdowns; long-term biomarker trend dashboards (labs + glucose metrics); program adherence and challenge progress screens; 'sneaky spikers vs steadier choices' comparisons. Trend/reference presentation is well-developed and copied industry-wide.
ux.engagement_channel: Daily feedback loops rather than transactional result-checking: instant meal->glucose feedback, Habit Loops with daily targets, metabolic checklist, streaks/adherence tracking, challenges, personalized insight nudges in-app. Channel: push + email newsletter; content moat (huge SEO blog, podcast 'A Whole New Level', member stories); referrals program. No community forum, no WhatsApp (US market). Retention is behavior-loop-driven — the app keeps value even between sensor wears (macro logging, habits) — explicitly designed against 'wear CGM once and churn'.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Claims rest on retrospective real-world member data, clearly labeled 'not a clinical trial, no control group': among 894 members with HbA1c >5.7%, 81% improved (avg -0.44pp, ~12% dropped >=0.6pp); among 164 with fasting insulin >18.4 uU/mL, 79% improved (avg -11.9); among 492 with insulin >10, 73% improved (avg -4.3); among 370 with triglycerides >150, 84% improved (73% by >=30 mg/dL). Honest labeling, but self-selected cohorts, no peer-reviewed publication of the 'largest observational glucose study' claim [uncertain]. Advisors shown: David Perlmutter MD and Robert Lustig MD — famous but polarizing figures; clinical review by licensed 'Levels-verified' clinicians (human-in-loop) is a genuine trust asset; HIPAA + SOC 2 claims; refund and replacement policies published. Pricing fully transparent (public price page). Risks: outcome marketing from uncontrolled data; advisor credibility contested (McGill's Jonathan Jarry: 'she is not a metabolic health expert' re: Means); MAHA-politics association may repel half the market.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Deliberate wellness-not-medical-device posture, enforced by a footer disclaimer on every page: 'intended only for maintaining and encouraging a healthy lifestyle... not to be used for the diagnosis, cure, management, prevention, or treatment of any disease... should never be used for medication management or dosing decisions.' History: originally CGMs prescribed off-label to non-diabetics via telehealth [uncertain on current prescription flow]; the 2024 FDA clearance of Dexcom's OTC Stelo (for adults not on insulin) let Levels move to an OTC sensor and drop the prescription friction — the regulatory risk was outsourced to the hardware maker. Not positioned as SaMD anywhere; no diagnostic claims; dietitian coaching billed as wellness. HSA/FSA via Truemed letters of medical necessity. US-only — no LGPD/ANVISA exposure, but also no international playbook. (For Dr. Exame: the 'never diagnose, educate + compare to reference ranges' line is the same compliance choice, executed with lawyer-grade consistency on every surface.)
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they do NOT do (Dr. Exame openings): no family/dependents/caregiver mode, no pediatric ranges, no hereditary-risk view (single-user only); no doctor-facing workflow — external physicians get bare viewer access, no consult brief/SOAP/summary export tailored to a visit; no chat-with-your-own-results AI inside the product (LevelsAI is a content-search bot, not a personal-data interpreter); no lab-partner/LIS or FHIR/records ingestion — you either buy their panel or upload files; no chronic-disease management (by design); US-only, English-only, premium price ($499-$1,999/yr + hardware economics unavailable in Brazil); single organ-system focus (metabolic) vs whole-panel interpretation. What works (inspiration, not copy): instant cause-effect feedback as the retention engine (food -> glucose -> score -> swap); membership bundling of hardware + 2 labs/yr + clinician review with a cheap app entry tier to widen funnel; publishing real-world outcome data (even retrospective, honestly labeled) as conversion marketing; HSA/FSA to soften price; quiz-first onboarding; keeping value between sensor wears so the app never feels transactional.
trust_gaps.relevance: High — this is the reference model for continuous engagement on top of health data: Levels converts lab numbers into a daily behavior loop (food -> glucose -> score -> habit), which is exactly the 'comportamento continuo' pattern Dr. Exame wants for retention. Direct product overlap with Dr. Exame is low (CGM hardware-led, metabolic-only, US premium D2C), so threat to a Brazil play is minimal; value is as an engagement-mechanics benchmark (streaks, habit loops, challenges, reassessment cadence, transparent outcome marketing) and as proof that bundling interpretation + cadence + humans sustains a >$1,000/yr consumer price.
